knowledge_gaps: The formula measures pair freshness, not witness freshness: when j<i, max(i,j)=i, so an arbitrarily old witness receives no additional age penalty relative to a newer witness preceding the same anchor. Rename the mechanism or justify this asymmetry.

The proposed comparisons do not isolate corroboration freshness from stronger recency weighting and reduced residual strength. Add a matched anchor-decay control and report support mass, clipping frequency, and residual norms.

An efficient implementation is unspecified. The reference loops cost O(BL³) before embedding pooling. For a fixed retained window, support can instead update as s[t,i]=max(exp(-1/rho_witness)*s[t-1,i], S[i,t]) for existing anchors, with separately initialized new anchors and eligibility masks. Sliding-window expiration requires additional handling.

Reproduction still requires executable baseline integration, an unambiguous inherited TF–IDF configuration and token pattern, resolved training/checkpoint settings, predictor signatures, and a prespecified budget allocation. Initial prediction parity also requires preserving baseline initialization and random-number consumption.

No validation results establish that stale corroboration is a material failure mode. Positional age cannot measure elapsed-time staleness or seasonality. Lexical duplicates, boilerplate, repeated historical positions, and metadata coverage remain possible shortcuts.

Originality 4 and potential 7 are provisional judgments without direct temporal-recommendation comparisons or validation evidence. Difficulty 4 appears optimistic for complete training, sparse text processing, diagnostics, and predictor integration.
